falsifier: replay.py or run.py's replay command filters cases through diagnosable or tuning_cases, or the printed targets name no holdout case
hypothesis: replay does not consult diagnosable, so a replay over an archive that holds cases 14 and 15 prints their fates, their candidates and their names in the targets list, against the rule that no diagnosis reads a holdout case (#744)
intervention: replayed evals/runs/20261005T-revert/main-r1..r5.json (15 cases) and read the output: the targets list names 14-loyalty-oauth-platform and 15-multitenant-invoicing with their fates. grep of evals/harness/replay.py for holdout finds nothing; lane_replay.py and critic_replay.py call refuse_holdout, and score's loss attribution skips a case that is not diagnosable. This audit read both holdout cases through that output, and records the read here
reconsider_when: replay skips a holdout case with a printed reason, through diagnosable, and a test holds it there
scope: the replay command at this revision over any archive that holds a holdout case; the two holdout cases are 14 and 15. Says nothing about score, which already skips them
signature: run.py replay reads a holdout case's emissions and prints its per-element losses

falsifier: a run's emission carries no flow from the actor at all, or carries one to the corpus destination under another label that the alignment could not pair
hypothesis: the flows every run omits are not unread sentences: the run carries the same interaction from the same actor, written to a dashboard, console or app process it added, or in the opposite direction, so a prompt edit that asks the model to read more has a ceiling of zero on them
intervention: read the per-run fates and extras of the five main-r* sweeps for the two flows omitted 5 of 5 times on development cases. Case 02 query-dashboards: every run writes fleet-operator>process:dashboard>view-dashboards plus process:dashboard>store:telemetry-lake, and process:dashboard is an extra element. Case 13 load-console: every run writes process:corporate-web-host>process:dispatch-console>serve-console, the host as initiator, and finds the corpus's open-console flow. Case 16 (one end-to-end run, evals/runs/20261010T-87-case16): member>process:library-app>use-app and library-app>lending-api>submit-request stand for the corpus's member>lending-api>borrow-renew-and-reserve; the source says members act through the library app on their phones. Omitted flow-runs on development cases: 20 of 5 sweeps, 16 of them on targets recurring 3 or more times; flow found sd 2.51 a sweep. No STRIDE claim in case 02 or 13 names the omitted flow; in case 16 six references and three must-finds rest on it, on one run
reconsider_when: extract.md gains a rule on who initiates the load of a browser or phone application, or a corpus ruling pairs the UI-process reading with the corpus flow
scope: development cases 02 and 13 over five extraction runs at 1de3337a on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna, and case 16 on one end-to-end run; the holdout cases are not read. Says which flows are lost and how, not what a prompt rule would make the model write
signature: extraction writes an actor's flow to a UI process it introduces, not to the component the corpus names as the destination

falsifier: model.json records a trust_zone assumption for each member of the omitted zone, or facts.json records the member's network-membership as stated
hypothesis: the boundary omissions are placements the signed reference itself calls inferred; placeholder_zones reads only model.json's trust_zone assumptions, and those cases record none, so the two readers of one placement disagree and the model is charged for following the placement rule
intervention: read the omitted boundary-runs on development cases: 09 customer-device 5 of 5, 04 public-internet 3, 01 public-internet 2, 07 internet 1. facts.json, signed mstarks01: 09 entity:customer and process:mobile-app inferred; 01 entity:shopper and entity:card-processor inferred; 04 entity:calling-service inferred; 07 entity:public-package-registry stated. model.json trust_zone assumptions: only 09 process:mobile-app. So 10 of the 11 omitted boundary-runs are zones whose every member is placed by an inferred row, and only case 07's is a miss. verify_corpus.py holds nothing between the two files
reconsider_when: the maintainer records the three cases' inferred placements as model.json assumptions, or a lint holds a signed inferred membership row to a model.json assumption
scope: the four zones named, on the five main-r* sweeps; development cases only. Measurement only: no job reads the corpus, so nothing live moves
signature: replay charges a zone as omitted where every member's signed membership row reads inferred

falsifier: the respelled candidate differs in type from the reference, a second same-type candidate exists, or the endpoint_unaligned flows rest on an endpoint that is not respelled
hypothesis: two plurals the sources themselves use, shoppers (case 01) and game servers (case 06), carry most of the endpoint losses on development cases; extract.md rule 3 already asks for the singular and the model obeys it in two runs of five on each, so the loss is a pairing decision and not a prompt gap
intervention: read the fates: respelled 8 element-runs on development cases (entity:shopper 3, process:game-server 3, entity:developer 1, 1 other), each with one same-type candidate under the plural slug; endpoint_unaligned 26 flow-runs, of which 15 are flows through those two plurals (case 06 four flows in three runs, case 01 one flow in three runs). The 2026-09-14 archive shows the same two. rule 3 of prompts/extract.md states the singular with the example sensor node, not sensor nodes

scope: development cases over the five main-r* sweeps at 1de3337a; measurement only, since a job never compares its names with the corpus. Says nothing about whether pairing a plural is right in every case
signature: an element written in the source's plural reads respelled, and every flow through it reads endpoint_unaligned
